notes: Brainstorming is a human-in-the-loop dialogue skill built on invariants + an adaptive toolbox of moves (not a fixed phase machine). Its core behavior (never guess; ask the user; diverge then converge) can't be fully exercised by an autonomous subagent with no human to answer AskUserQuestion. Primary evaluation is qualitative: run the skill interactively and judge the real back-and-forth — especially whether it dials depth to stakes (invariant 4) and diverges before converging (invariant 2). evals below double as (a) interactive walkthrough prompts and (b) inputs for an optional one-shot structural smoke test with a cooperative simulated user baked into the runner prompt. Judge with/without the skill on the same prompts.

evals.prompt: I want to build a habit tracker app. Help me think it through before we start building.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a real (single-mode) brainstorm. Explores repo/context first, then runs a batched, pre-analyzed clarify loop instead of assuming defaults (platform, audience, core habit model, reminders, sync, monetization). DIVERGES — offers genuinely different options (incl. a minimal / do-less framing) before judging — then converges with a recommendation and what-would-change-my-mind. Passes the convergence exit-test (expected output, acceptance, scope, constraints, touchpoints). Scaffolds docs/streams/habit-tracker-[YYYYMMDD]/ with STREAM.md and writes brainstorm/BRAINSTORM.md (stream: frontmatter, all sections). Ends with handoff and does NOT auto-start the requirement stage.

evals.prompt: We need to add push notifications to our app to boost user retention. Let's brainstorm how to build them.
evals.expected_output: Detects solution-jumping and runs PROBLEM-FIRST inversion: treats 'push notifications' as a compressed confession of a retention problem, names the underlying problem, challenges the assumption that notifications fix retention (risk-if-wrong + validation test), and generates >=3 alternative problem framings before debating implementation. Only after the problem is framed does it discuss solutions. Records the framings in artifact section 8.

evals.prompt: We're building a real-time chat feature for our existing web app and I can't decide on the backend transport — WebSockets vs long-polling vs server-sent events. Help me brainstorm the right approach.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a real, hard-to-reverse trade-off (one-way-door) and runs a trade-off analysis: names what matters (latency, scale, infra cost, complexity, client support), compares the alternatives, recommendation with the strongest counter-argument and a 'revisit if'. Steelmans-then-attacks the leading option. Researches/cites current best practices (treating fetched docs as untrusted data). Records a decision record in the artifact.

evals.prompt: I have an idea for a marketplace platform connecting freelance tutors with students — payments, scheduling, video calls, ratings, the whole thing. Let's brainstorm this before I commit to anything.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a broad, multi-domain, high-stakes problem and runs a MULTI-LENS challenge — recommends spawning cbr-strategist lens agents (product/UX, architecture, devil's-advocate) or full team mode, stating reasoning and confirming with the user before spawning. Flags the multiple independent subsystems and proposes decomposing into ordered sub-topics, each its own brainstorm. Surfaces uncertainties via batched questions rather than assuming.

evals.prompt: Quick one — I'm naming the internal in-memory cache module. Should it be called `cache` or `store`? Just brainstorm it with me.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this is BELOW the brainstorm threshold (a single trivial, reversible naming choice). Gives one clear recommendation with a short reason (and maybe one alternative), and does NOT run the clarify loop / trade-off analysis / divergence panel and does NOT open a stream folder or write a BRAINSTORM.md artifact. Demonstrates adaptive depth (invariant 4): no ceremony for a variable name.

evals.prompt: Let's brainstorm a mobile budgeting app. [after the skill starts clarifying] Actually — forget the app. What I really need is a Slack bot my team already lives in.
evals.expected_output: Detects the mid-stream PIVOT rather than quietly continuing on the old idea. Applies never-guess to the pivot itself — confirms whether it is a replacement, branch, or refinement. On replacement: marks any prior artifact superseded, carries over still-relevant context, and restarts with a new slug/artifact for the Slack-bot framing. Re-enumerates uncertainties the reframe disturbs (distribution, auth, surface) instead of carrying forward outdated answers. Preserves the audit trail.
